Record pass when loaded.
r0-context.finding: Loaded global-crew.md + global-everyone.md (inherited doctrine), ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md (no CREW_CONTEXT.md/GLOSSARY.md in this repo), the g1 handoff, g1-implement-result.md, the full diff 967493c..HEAD (checklist_engine.py, episode_capture.py, test_episode_capture.py), context_manifest.py, agent_work_root.py and install_constellation.py.

r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding: Task statement satisfied in the source repo (emit from start/reopen, write-if-absent, logic in a separate module, fail-soft-not-silent, durable=checkout root) and criteria 2/3/4 verified independently. FAILS close criterion 1: I constructed a sequence reaching advance with no emit. No skill in install_constellation.SKILL_SCRIPT_BUNDLES ships episode_capture.py, context_manifest.py or agent_work_root.py, and the engine's 'except ImportError -> return None' degrades to a SILENT no-op. Reproduced on the real installed reviewer skill engine: start g1 -> exit 0, advance g1 -> exit 0 -> complete, ZERO manifests, no stderr. Every installed skill is that case.

r2-scope.title: Scope drift
r2-scope.imperative: Did the change stay inside allowed scope and respect specific exclusions? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r2-scope.finding: No scope drift. git diff 967493c..HEAD touches exactly scripts/checklist_engine.py, scripts/episode_capture.py, tests/test_episode_capture.py. dispatch(), main(), context_manifest.py, apply_episode_delta.py, query_episodes.py, run.dirty and the refusals counter are all untouched; no roots CLI flag. git status --porcelain shows nothing stranded except this review's own artifacts. The two reopen base_dir plumbing lines exceed the literal 'import plus two call sites' criterion; I accept the Commander's ruling (alternatives are worse) but record that they buy nothing on any reachable production path -- see r4.

r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Every claim reproduced at its source, none accepted on assertion. (a) Full suite: I ran python -m pytest tests/ -q and got 1435 passed, 2 skipped, 409 subtests in 80.10s - exactly the claim. (b) Exit-code parity: I extracted the pre-seam engine independently via 'git show 967493c:scripts/checklist_engine.py' (verified it contains no emit_step_manifest) and ran 17 case/verb pairs through both binaries - 17/17 identical exit codes AND identical stdout/stderr, including 7 cases the implementer never ran (root-escaping path, glob path, non-list declaration, bare-string entry, null work_id, survey record, directory-as-declared-file). (c) The non-null durable rev: verified at the RESOLVED ABSOLUTE PATH on all three durable_root branches. (d) write-if-absent: sha256 AND mtime_ns both identical across advance+reopen with the declaration genuinely swapped underneath; manifest still records the original declaration. (e) files:null vs files:[] : both produced by real emits and both read; both falsy, distinguishable by identity and by emit_error.

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: Handoff constraints: write-if-absent PASS (hash+mtime, changed declaration). Fail-soft-not-silent PASS at runtime (stub carries emit_error and files:null; both falsy, distinguishable by identity and by emit_error; the stub also lacks contract/repo_rev so it cannot be mistaken for a manifest). Emission-after-mutation PASS. No-logic-in-the-engine PASS with one exception (r8). FAILS the inherited 'Universal posture: no hidden fallback; fail visibly' and D8's own 'a non-reading must be visibly distinct from an uncollected one': the engine's 'except ImportError: def emit_step_manifest(...): return None' is a hidden fallback that produces NO file, NO stderr and NO exit-code change - the exact fail-silent shape D8 forbids at the runtime layer, reinstated at the packaging layer, and it is the operative path in every installed skill. Second, narrower fail: SURVEY checklists never emit at all - record() has no in-progress guard, so a survey completes and consolidates from pending with zero manifests (reproduced). D1's reachability argument is scoped to a gated spine; nothing states that scope limit where a reader would find it.

r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation check
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from the recorded architecture in a way Commander must reconcile? Record pass/fail; flag a triage candidate if it is out of scope.
r5-reconciliation.finding: Two divergences Commander must reconcile. (1) manifest_root()'s documented claim -- 'the manifest lands beside the spine it describes, inside the same work area' -- is FALSE for this repo's actual crew-checklist layout. It composes parent-of-checklist-dir + work_id, which only coincides with the work area when dirname(checklist)==work_id. Crew plans live at .agent-work/<issue>/crew/<gate>-plan.json, so the implementer's own manifests landed in .agent-work/issue-305/issue-305-g1-implement/ -- a phantom directory containing nothing but context/ -- and mine in .agent-work/issue-305/issue-305-g1-review/. The test fixture's own docstring concedes 'only this shape puts the manifest beside the spine'. That is untracked orphan scratch closeout is meant to find none of. (2) The import cycle context_manifest -> checklist_engine -> episode_capture is now real and is broken only by a function-local import; it is a durable constraint on the dependency graph and belongs in the map. Triage candidates: unguarded work_id in the manifest path (work_id '../../ESCAPED' writes outside the work area - reproduced); SKILL_ROOT in a skill-source repo makes every skill-rooted required:true row rev:null.

r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json, run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py <record> (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. Do NOT silently skip this item.
constraints: Fowler smells are subordinate to documented repo standards; never hard violations
an override (smell not flagged because a standard wins) needs a logged reason
r6-fowler.finding: Pass run and recorded at .agent-work/issue-305/g1-review/fowler-pass.json; scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py exits 0 (smells=12, flagged=2, overridden=5, absent=5). FLAGGED: duplicated-code (emit_step_manifest and _write_failure_stub carry the same four-step place-and-write sequence, and the two copies already disagree on which step id names the file -- manifest['step'] vs iid); shotgun-surgery (the change's true blast radius spans four sites and only three were landed -- install_constellation.SKILL_SCRIPT_BUNDLES was missed, which is the packaging blocker in smell form). OVERRIDDEN with logged standards: feature-envy (adapter-at-a-seam is the module's job, global-everyone Deep-module vocabulary + D1); data-clumps (the (cl,iid,base_dir) triple is the engine's own pre-existing verb signature, global-crew match-surrounding-conventions); primitive-obsession (ROOT_TOKENS is #300's frozen JSON contract, D2 satisfy-as-written); speculative-generality (the public root helpers ARE the test surface criterion 3 demands, and are what made my mutants MUT-A/MUT-B killable); comments-as-deodorant (rationale-dense docstrings are the convention of every neighbouring module, and episode_capture.py:54-57 is the only record of the durable_agent_work trap). Neither flagged smell is a blocker on its own; shotgun-surgery is the same defect as r1.

r7-mutation.title: Independent mutation (mandatory)
r7-mutation.imperative: Devise at least one mutation the implementer did not ship, outside its set, and confirm the suite catches it.
r7-mutation.finding: SIX mutants run, FIVE of them outside the implementer's set (its mutants were: stub writes files:[]; failed emit returns None). All six KILLED, against tests/test_episode_capture.py + test_context_manifest.py + test_checklist_engine.py (baseline 424 passed). MUT-A durable_root(repo)->durable_agent_work(repo), the exact double-nesting trap of criterion 3: killed, 4 tests. MUT-B durable_root(repo)->durable_root(base_dir), the spelling resolve_roots' own docstring warns against: killed, 3 tests. MUT-K reopen's emit moved BEFORE the status mutation, probing whether the load-bearing 'AFTER the mutation' comment is actually guarded: killed, Seam::test_seam_reopen_emits_the_manifest_too. MUT-C manifest_root drops .parent: killed, 5 tests. MUT-D write-if-absent guard removed (always overwrite): killed, Emit::test_emit_never_overwrites_an_already_present_manifest. MUT-E (control) emit removed from start(): killed, 3 tests. Working tree restored clean after every mutant (git diff --stat -- scripts/ empty). Conclusion: the shipped tests have genuine falsifiability on every code path this gate added -- I could not find a surviving mutant inside the diff. The one thing NO mutant can reach is the packaging path in r1: there is no test asserting that episode_capture.py ships with an engine-carrying skill, so deleting it from a bundle is a mutation the suite cannot see.

r8-engine-logic-free.title: Engine diff is genuinely logic-free (no machine check covered this)
r8-engine-logic-free.imperative: Form an independent verdict on whether scripts/checklist_engine.py gained only an import shim and call sites, no logic. The implementer's own check (git diff --stat) could not fail.
r8-engine-logic-free.finding: Independent verdict, read line by line rather than counted: the engine diff IS logic-free, with one genuine exception the Commander should know about. What landed: (1) sys.path.insert(0, <scripts dir>) at module scope; (2) a guarded 'from episode_capture import emit_step_manifest' with an ImportError no-op fallback; (3) one call line in start(); (4) one call line in reopen(); (5) base_dir added to reopen()'s signature; (6) _run_verb passing it. Items 3-6 carry no branch, no state, no decision -- every when/which-roots/where decision is in episode_capture.py, and I confirmed that by mutating the engine (MUT-E, MUT-K) and finding the failures land in seam tests, not in engine behavior tests. The exception is item 1: sys.path.insert is a process-global side effect now paid by every importer of checklist_engine, not just the CLI. There is precedent (context_manifest.py:79 does the same) and no name in scripts/ shadows a stdlib or third-party module today, so I do not block on it -- but it is the one line in this diff that is not inert, and it is the mechanism by which item 2's fallback silently swallows a partial install. On the Commander's flag A: the vacuous 'git diff --stat' check is correctly identified as no check at all; my read is independent and reaches the same acceptance, with item 1 named. On flag B (the two reopen plumbing lines): I ACCEPT them, but the stated justification is wrong. reopen() refuses any gate that is not 'complete', and a complete gate has necessarily passed start(), so its manifest already exists and write-if-absent returns early -- I reproduced this (sha256 AND mtime_ns identical across a reopen with the declaration genuinely swapped underneath). reopen's emit is a NO-OP on every reachable production path. Keep the lines (they are correct-by-symmetry with start(), cost nothing, and do fire for a pre-#305 spine or a deleted manifest), but record the real reason rather than 'without base_dir reopen could not emit'.

consolidation.summary: BLOCK on close criterion 1. The seam is correctly built, correctly tested and correctly scoped in the source repo -- criteria 2, 3 and 4 all verified independently, six mutants (five novel) all killed, full suite reproduced at 1435/2/409 -- but I constructed the sequence the criterion asks for: no skill in install_constellation.SKILL_SCRIPT_BUNDLES ships episode_capture.py, context_manifest.py or agent_work_root.py, and the engine's guarded import degrades to a SILENT no-op, so on the real installed reviewer-skill engine start+advance both exit 0, the gate completes, and zero manifests exist with nothing on stderr. Doctrine requires agents to run the installed copy, so that is the production path: the feature is inert everywhere it ships, and inert in exactly the fail-silent shape ruling D8 forbids. Secondary: survey checklists never emit at all (record() has no in-progress guard). Both are small fixes; neither is a rebuild.

triage_candidates.statement: manifest_root() composes parent-of-checklist-dir + work_id, so the manifest only lands in the work area when dirname(checklist)==work_id. This repo's crew checklists live at .agent-work/<issue>/crew/, so every crew manifest creates a phantom sibling directory (.agent-work/issue-305/issue-305-g1-implement/context/). Either derive the root from the checklist path alone, or make the mismatch visible.

work_id is composed into the manifest path unguarded: a checklist with work_id '../../ESCAPED' writes its manifest outside the work area (reproduced). Same for a step id containing separators. context_manifest.manifest_path is #300's frozen surface, so the guard belongs either there or in episode_capture.manifest_root.

SURVEY checklists never emit a manifest: record() has no in-progress guard, so a Reviewer/Cartographer/Curator/Scout survey completes and consolidates from pending with zero emits (reproduced). Either wire the seam for surveys or state the gated-only scope limit where the unskippability claim is made.

The engine never validates a checklist's initial statuses on load, so an authored/instantiated checklist whose gate already reads 'in-progress' advances with no emit (reproduced). Cheap fix: a load-time refusal of a non-pending initial status, or accept and document it.

episode_capture.emit_step_manifest and _write_failure_stub duplicate the place-and-write-if-absent sequence and already disagree on the step id that names the file (manifest['step'] vs iid). Extract a shared _place(checklist, base_dir, step).
